rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Fatiha because it opens the codex, instruction, Qur'an recitation, prayer, speech, revelation, the aims of this life, and the gates of Paradise.
rows.anchor: لافتتاح المصاحف والتعليم وقراءة القرآن والصلاة بها وإما لأن الحمد فاتحة كل كلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also a key to the Qur'an's treasures: knowledge of its meanings unlocks ambiguous passages and illuminates its verses.
rows.anchor: لأنها مفتاح كنوز لطائف الخطاب بانجلائها ينكشف جميع القرآن لأهل البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatiha is the Mother of the Qur'an because it gathers the Qur'an's purposes: affirming divinity and prophethood, and establishing decree and predestination.
rows.anchor: أربعة : إقرار بالألوهية والنبوة وإثبات القضاء والقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening praise and names of the Merciful indicate God's divinity.
rows.anchor: {الحمد لله رب العالمين * الرحمن الرحيم} يدل على الألوهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the seven oft-repeated because it has seven verses, each can stand for seven Qur'anic portions, and reciting them is said to earn the whole Qur'an's reward or close seven gates of Hell.
rows.anchor: لأنها سبع آيات أو لأن كل آية منها تقوم مقام سبع من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-mathani is explained by repetition in prayer or each rak'a, intercession in each rak'a, or revelation twice, in Mecca and Medina.
rows.anchor: فلأنها تثنى في كل صلاة أو في كل ركعة بالنسبة إلى الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other names include the Prayer, Healing, Cure, Foundation, Sufficient, Complete, Praise, Supplication, Thanks, and Invocation surahs because their meanings occur in it.
rows.anchor: وسميت بسورة الصلاة وسورة الشفاء والشافية وأساس القرآن والكافية والوافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the Treasure surah because a report says the Opening is a treasure from God's Throne.
rows.anchor: وسورة الكنز لما يروى أن الله تعالى قال : "فاتحة الكتاب كنز من كنوز عرشي"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A day ordinarily runs from sunrise to sunset, and legally from dawn to sunset; here it means time in general because the Judgment has no sun.
rows.anchor: اليوم في العرف عبارة عما بين طلوع الشمس وغروبها من الزمان وفي الشرع عما بين طلوع الفجر الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns the whole affair on the day of recompense; specifying that day magnifies it and shows His exclusive rule when all worldly ties of ownership end.
rows.anchor: أي مالك الأمر كله في يوم الجزاء فإضافة اليوم إلى الدين لأدنى ملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human ownership is figurative and partial, temporary, and confined to bodies and outward things; God's ownership is complete and never passes away.
rows.anchor: فلله في الحقيقة القوة الكاملة والولاية النافذة والحكم الجاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading Malik with the alif earns more reward than Maliki because it adds a letter, each Qur'anic letter earning ten good deeds.
rows.anchor: وقراءة مالك بالألف أكثر ثوابا من ملك لزيادة حرف فيه

rows.speaker: محمد بن شجاع الثلجي
rows.claim: Muhammad b. Shuja' dreamed that omitting the alif cost ten merits, then dreamed that majestic recitation also supported his original reading.
rows.anchor: يحكى عن أبي عبد الله محمد بن شجاع الثلجي رحمه الله تعالى أنه قال : كان من عادتي قراءة مالك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The cited report promises ten good deeds for every Qur'anic letter and urges reciting the Qur'an with solemn grandeur.
rows.anchor: أما سمعت قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "من قرأ القرآن كتب له بكل حرف عشر حسنات

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub distinguishes a malik, who owns something in the world, from a malek, who rules kings.
rows.anchor: فأتيت قطربا وكان إماما في اللغة فسألته ما بين المالك والملك فقال : بينهما فرق كثير

rows.speaker: أهل الحرمين
rows.claim: The two Holy Cities' readers use Maliki, meaning sovereign dominion, irresistible control, and authority over public affairs, which best fits the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحرمين المحترمين ملك من الملك الذي هو عبارة عن السلطان القاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five divine attributes unfold a sequence: God creates, nurtures with favors, conceals sin in mercy, forgives repentance, and finally judges.
rows.anchor: خلقتك فأنا إله ثم ربيتك بالنعم فأنا رب ثم عصيت فسترت عليك فأنا رحمن

rows.speaker: النجمي
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading takes din as Islam, citing 3:19, and distinguishes outward bodily submission from inward, luminous surrender to God's eternal decree.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" الإشارة في {مالك يوم الدين} أن الدين في الحقيقة الإسلام

rows.speaker: النجمي
rows.claim: The bodily form of Islam is likened to night and the heart's inward Islam to daylight; spiritual awakening lets the seeker recognize the sole King of Judgment.
rows.anchor: فإسلام الظاهر بإقرار اللسان وعمل الأركان فهذا الإسلام جسداني والجسداني ظلماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker advances from the darkness of the self to certainty that no one owns or rules except the Owner of Judgment Day, then addresses Him directly in worship.
rows.anchor: فيشاهد بعين اليقين بل يكاشف حق اليقين أن الملكولا مالك إلا مالك يوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disobeying a king can disorder the world, so subjects should obey rulers and rulers should obey the King of kings; obedience preserves worldly welfare.
rows.anchor: فعلى الرعية مطاوعة الملوك وعلى الملوك مطاوعة ملك الملوك لينتظم مصالح العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's perfect kingship includes justice: on Judgment Day He sets just scales and no soul is wronged.
rows.anchor: ومن لطائفه أيضا أن مالك يوم الدين يبين أن كمال ملكه بعدله حيث قال : {ونضع الموازين القسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Anushirwan's fruit turned sour when he contemplated unjustly seizing an orchard, then sweet after he repented, illustrating how justice sustains prosperity.
rows.anchor: يحكى أن أنوشروان انقطع في الصيد عن القوم فانتهى إلى بستان

rows.speaker: الفناري
rows.claim: Al-Fanari suggests the Prophet's reported pride in being born under a just king referred to the era's spiritual light and Anushirwan's relative justice.
rows.anchor: قال الفناري في تفسير الفاتحة : بل لعله تفاخر بزمنه النوراني حتى ولد فيه مثله

rows.speaker: الإمام السخاوي
rows.claim: Al-Sakhawi says the report about being born in a just king's era has no basis or authenticity; if valid, it names Anushirwan rather than certifying his justice.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام السخاوي في "المقاصد الحسنة" حديث : "ولدت في زمن الملك العادل" لا أصل له ولا صحة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says an unjust governor will be cast onto Hell's bridge; if disobedient, it breaks and he falls for fifty years.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "يجاء بالوالي يوم القيامة فينبذ به على جسر جهنم

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Sa'di's verses warn that a tyrant's injustice will not endure and leaves a lasting curse upon him.
rows.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره : مهازور مندى مكن برجهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah moves from signs and reflection on divine names to the endpoint of the knower's journey: direct witnessing and intimate address.
rows.anchor: بنى الله سبحانه أول الكلام على ما هو مبادي حال العارف من الذكر والفكر والتأمل في أسمائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshipper should attend first to God, seeing worship as a noble connection to Him rather than as a deed owned by the self.
rows.anchor: أن العابد ينبغي أن يكون نظره إلى المعبود أولا وبالذات ومنه إلى العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intimate assurance that God is with the Prophet in the cave surpasses Moses' statement that his Lord will guide him.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فضل ما حكى عن حبيبه حين قال : {لا تحزن إن الله معنا}

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says worship wherever used in the Qur'an means monotheism, tasbih means prayer, and qunut means obedience.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة : جميع ما ذكر في القرآن من العبادة التوحيد

rows.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Gabriel told the Prophet to understand You alone we worship as placing hope in God alone.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن جبريل عليه السلام قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قل يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun can include the prayer leader and those present, including recording angels, or all monotheists whose worship and needs the reciter joins.
rows.anchor: والضمير المستكن في {نعبد} وكذا في {نستعين} للقارىء ومن معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This collective form helps explain why congregational prayer was prescribed: the individual folds his worship and need into the community's.
rows.anchor: أوله ولسائر الموحدين أدرج عبادته في تضاعيف عبادتهم وخلط حاجته بحاجتهم

rows.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi explains the plural as gathering the human person's subtle center with its body and parts, each of which owes fitting worship to God.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ الأكبر والمسك الأذفر قدسنا الله بسره الأطهر في كتاب "العظمة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship belongs exclusively to God because its ultimate reverence is due only to the greatest benefactor, who creates the beneficiary and gives life.
rows.anchor: وإنما خصص العبادة به تعالى لأن العبادة نهاية التعظيم فلا تليق إلا بالمنعم في الغاية

rows.speaker: الصدر القونوي
rows.claim: Qunawi calls the servant sincere when he witnesses God as the source of action and attribution, and fully realized when that witness encompasses every state without heedlessness.
rows.anchor: كذا في تفسير الفاتحة للصدر القنوي قدس سره

rows.speaker: النجمي
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading says the shift from speaking of God to addressing Him directly occurs when the seeker crosses the veil of owning the self.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" في قوله : {إياك نعبد} رجع إلى الخطاب من الغيبة

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد
rows.claim: Abu Yazid's unveiling gives the way to God as abandoning the self and coming to Him.
rows.anchor: كما قال أبو يزيد في بعض مكاشفاته : إلهي كيف السبيل إليك؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi relays the Najmiyya interpretation that the self has four faculties, matched by four divine attributes that draw the servant toward God.
rows.anchor: فللنفس أربع صفات : أمارة ، ولوامة ، وملهمة ، ومطمئنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God remembers the tranquil soul as promised in 2:152, calls it back to Him, and draws it from absence of self into witnessing its Lord's ownership.
rows.anchor: ويناديه ويخاطب نفسه {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة}

rows.speaker: النجمي
rows.claim: A person who reaches witnessing his Lord sees the beauty of his true Owner and addresses Him as a humbled, helpless servant; some read Malik as a vocative.
rows.anchor: فيشاهد جمال مالكه ويناديه نداء عبد خاضع خاشع ذليل عاجز

rows.speaker: النجمي
rows.claim: The soul serves worldly desire, the heart serves Paradise, the spirit seeks nearness, and the secret worships God alone.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن النفس دنيوية تعبد هواها الدنيوي لقوله تعالى : {أفرءيت من اتخذ إلاهه هوااه} (الجاثية : 23) والقلب أخروي يعبد الجنة لقوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: النجمي
rows.claim: A sacred report calls sincerity a secret between God and His servant that no angel or messenger can enter.
rows.anchor: لقوله تعالى على لسان نبيه عليه السلام : "الإخلاص سر بيني وبين عبدي

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sacred report says prayer is divided between God and His servant, who receives what he asks.
rows.anchor: قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل

rows.speaker: النجمي
rows.claim: The servant approaches through praise and gratitude, while God draws him away from other attachments into divine unity and witnessing.
rows.anchor: فتقرب العبد بنصفه إلى حضرة كماله بالحمد والثناء والشكر على صفات جماله وجلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking help means asking God for aid in worship, in what exceeds our power, against Satan, and in the needs of worldly and religious life.
rows.anchor: والاستعانة طلب العون ويعدى بالباء وبنفسه أي : تطلب العون على عبادتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two phrases mean serving and asking help from God alone.
rows.anchor: ثم تحقيقهما من العبد أن لا يخدم غير الله ولا يسأل إلا من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing worship before the request follows the verse endings and teaches that presenting a means before asking a need is more likely to bring an answer.
rows.anchor: أدعى إلى الإجابة وإياك نعبد لما أورثه العجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairing worship with dependence combines pride in serving God with humility about needing His aid, and removes worshipper's conceit.
rows.anchor: إياك نعبد لما أورثه العجب أردف إياك نستعين إزالة له وإفناء للنخوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing expresses Sunni teaching: the servant performs actions while God creates and grants success, rejecting both Jabriyya denial of human action and Mu'tazila denial of divine aid.
rows.anchor: إذ فيه إثبات الفعل من العبد والتوفيق من الله كالخلق

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan fainted while leading prayer at this verse, fearing that his appeal to God alone would be contradicted by seeking physicians' or rulers' doors.
rows.anchor: حكي عن سفيان الثوري رحمه الله أنه أم قوما في صلاة المغرب فلما قال : {إياك نعبد

rows.speaker: الخليل عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abraham declined Gabriel's offer of help in the catapult, saying God already knew his state; the author likens his own restraint and reliance to Abraham's.
rows.anchor: اقتداء بالخليل عليه السلام في قيد النمرود حيث قال له جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guide us to the straight path spells out the requested help, and supplication after completing worship is a religious practice.
rows.anchor: بيان المعونة المطلوبة كأنه قيل : كيف أعينك؟

rows.speaker: التيسير
rows.claim: The Taysir commentary reads worship as affirming divine unity, seeking help as asking aid for it, and guidance as asking steadfastness in religion.
rows.anchor: قال في "التيسير" : {إياك نعبد} إظهار التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Steadfast guidance is among the greatest needs, sought by prophets, Pharaoh's magicians, and the Companions; outward devotion cannot guarantee one's final state.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن الثبات على الهداية أهم الحاجات إذ هو الذي سأله الأنبياء والأولياء كما قال يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The seeker who has reached God still asks for guidance through Him, because the journey in God has no endpoint while knowledge and divine possibilities remain without limit.
rows.anchor: وفي "تفسير القاضي" إذا قاله العارف الواصل إلى الله عنى به

rows.speaker: الفناري
rows.claim: Al-Fanari explains the continuing journey by saying that knowledge and what God can do have no limit, so the servant's longing never ends.
rows.anchor: قال المولى الفناري : ومبناه أن السير في الله غير متناه كما قال قطب المحققين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Straight path is a metaphor for Islam and true religion, likened to a physical route because a seeker must cross distances and endure obstacles to arrive.
rows.anchor: والصراط المستقيم استعارة عن ملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the guided ask for the balanced middle in desire, anger, and spending, and for insight into how every thing points to God's essence, attributes, and acts.
rows.anchor: أن لا بد بعد معرفة الله تعالى والاهتداء بها من معرفة الخط المتوسط بين الإفراط والتفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading of guidance is to turn from everything besides God and wholly obey Him, even under Abraham's, Ishmael's, Jonah's, Moses', or John and Zechariah's severe commands.
rows.anchor: طلب الإعراض عما سوى الله وإن كان نفسه والإقبال بالكلية عليه حتى لو أمر بذبح ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the path that of people God favored, rather than people killed or punished, softens the demand and invites believers toward prophetic and saintly states.
rows.anchor: دون أن يقول صراط الذين ضربوا وقتلوا تيسيرا ما وترغيبا إلى مقام الأنبياء والأولياء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that Surah Hud and its sisters made him gray because he was commanded to remain steadfast.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "شيبتني هود وأخواتها" حيث ورد فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Steadfastness means moderation between excess and neglect across natural and spiritual traits; the law sets this balance in action, speech, money, and character.
rows.anchor: فإن الإنسان من حيث نشأته وقواه الظاهرة والباطنة مشتمل على صفات

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet advised a would-be ascetic to fast and break fast, pray and sleep, because his self, wife, and visitors each had rights.
rows.anchor: إن لنفسك عليك حقا ولزوجك عليك حقا ولزورك عليك حقا فصم وأفطر وقم ونم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Umar recited loudly to wake sleepers and repel Satan, the Prophet told him to lower his voice slightly; he told Abu Bakr, who prayed softly, to raise his slightly.
rows.anchor: ولما رأى صلى الله عليه وسلم عمر رضي الله عنه يقرأ رافعا صوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author grades spiritual integrity by combinations of heart, action, and speech: complete inward and outward integrity is highest, while integrity in only one or two can harm its holder.
rows.anchor: والمستقيم على أقسام منها : مستقيم بقوله وفعله وقلبه ومستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those You favored is a complete substitution for the first straight path; favor here means the religion's beneficial gift.
rows.anchor: {صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم} بدل من الأول بدل الكل والإنعام إيصال النعمة

rows.speaker: أبو العباس بن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata assigns knowledge to knowers, truthfulness, contentment, certainty and purity to saints, patience and compassion to the righteous, obedience's sweetness to seekers, and steadfastness to believers.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العباس بن عطاء : هؤلاء المنعم عليهم هم طبقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another identification, matching 4:69, is prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and the righteous.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : {فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهدآء والصالحين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path belongs to God by law and choice, and to servants as something they follow and obey; both attributions express its relationship to each side.
rows.anchor: وسره من وجوه : الأول : بيان أن ذلك كله له شرعا ولنا نفعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the path to God cuts off the servant's vanity; attributing it to the servant comforts and honors him, and removes Satan's hope of stripping believers of dignity.
rows.anchor: أنه أضافه إلى نفسه قطعا لعجب العبد وإلى العبد تسلية لقلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating path indicates two journeys: the frightening way from servant to Lord, where caravans and mounts are lost, and the way from Lord to servant.
rows.anchor: وتكرار الصراط إشارة إلى أن الصراط الحقيقي صراطان : من العبد إلى الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not those angered or astray substitutes for those favored, describing the favored as free of anger and misguidance; ghayr can mean different from, not, or except.
rows.anchor: وكلمة غير على ثلاثة أوجه : الأول : بمعنى المغايرة وفارسيته "جز"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine anger cannot mean its human beginning, so it denotes its end or effect, such as punishment, retribution, or painful seizure.
rows.anchor: أن القاعدة التفسيرية أن الأفعال التي لها أوائل بدايات وأواخر غايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance means deliberately or accidentally leaving the sound path; sinners fail in action, while the ignorant fail in knowledge.
rows.anchor: والضلال : العدول عن الطريق السوي عمدا أو خطأ ، والمراد بالمغضوب عليهم العصاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A common reading identifies those angered as Jews and those astray as Christians, but neither group's label is exclusive because Scripture attributes both traits to both.
rows.anchor: أو المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود لقوله تعالى في حقهم : {من لعنه الله وغضب عليه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anger fits the Jews especially because of their rebellious unbelief, aggression, killing prophets, and saying God is poor while they are rich.
rows.anchor: بل المراد أنهما إذا تقابلا فالتعبير بالغضب الذي هو إرادة الانتقام لا محالة باليهود أليق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning both groups after the favored expresses full fear alongside the hope of favor; the Prophet says a believer's fear and hope balance.
rows.anchor: فائدته وصف إيمانهم بكمال الخوف من حال الطائفتين بعد وصفه بكمال الرجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine anger perfects the function of the left hand: mercy and severity have distinct effects, and severity completes what cannot be repaired by mercy.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن حكم الغضب الإلهي تكميل مرتبة قبضة الشمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anger also purifies, like a doctor cutting a diseased limb or fire separating gold from lead and copper.
rows.anchor: والسر الثالث التطهير كالذهب الممزوج بالرصاص والنحاس إذا قصد تمييزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bewilderment has blameworthy and praiseworthy forms; a beginner resolves confusion by identifying the goal, sound path, guide, helpful practices, and obstacles.
rows.anchor: والضلال هو الحيرة فمنها ما هي مذمومة ومنها ما هي محمودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bewilderment of advanced knowers is not a defect but appears after perfected knowledge, witnessing, and insight into the secret of existence.
rows.anchor: وحيرة الأكابر محمودة لا تظنن أن هذه الحيرة سببها قصور في الإدراك

rows.speaker: النجمي
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading describes the two groups as people who missed divine light and wandered in the self's desires, nature's darkness, and imitation.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير النجم {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضآلين} هم الذين أخطأهم ذلك النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih means declaring transcendence; some scholars say divine names are fixed by revelation, and al-A'la most clearly describes the Lord rather than the name.
rows.anchor: التسبيح التنزيه واسم الله لا يصح أن يطلق عليه بالنظر إلى ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's height is beyond the grasp of describers and knowers, not spatial elevation or bodily size; recognizing His majesty should humble worshippers.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم ليس علوه عو جهة ولا كبره كبر جثة سبحانه عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command forbids treating al-A'la as spatial height, istiwa as settling, or divine names as shared with idols and false claimants such as Musaylima.
rows.anchor: نزه اسمه عن الإلحاد فيه بالتأويلات الزائغة نحو أن يجعل الأعلى من العلو في المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reverence requires avoiding careless mention of God's name, including while yawning or relieving oneself, and careless, excessive swearing.
rows.anchor: وكذا نزهه عن ذكره لا عى وجه الإعظام والإجلال

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir glosses the command as raising one's voice in remembrance of God's name, indicating that the word name is meaningful rather than redundant.
rows.anchor: وقال جرير في الآية ارفع صوتك بذكره أي بذكر اسمه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some commentators take name and named as one here, understanding the command to purify God's essence from imagination.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم الاسم والمسمى هنا واحد أي نزه ذاته عما دخل في الوهم والخيال

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet assigned the phrase glorify your Lord, the Magnificent to bowing and glorify your Lord, the Most High to prostration.
rows.anchor: في الحديث لما نزلت فسبح باسم ربك العظيم قال عليه السلام اجعلوها في ركوعكم

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Sa'di al-Mufti says the hadith indicates that the word name is redundant and that saying Subhana Rabbi al-A'la fulfills the command.
rows.anchor: قاله سعدي المفتي وعلى أن الامتثال بالأمر يحصل بأن يقول سبحان ربي العظيم والأعلى

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani says the Highest and Greatest name is God's essence with all attributes; its special glorification is self-emptying until divine perfections appear.
rows.anchor: وقال القاشاني : اسمه الأعلى والأعظم هو الذات مع جميع الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each creature has its own form of glorification.
rows.anchor: ولك شيء تسبيح خاص يسبح به اسما خالصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created everything and proportioned it by giving each thing what enables its perfection and sustenance.
rows.anchor: فسوى خلقه بأن جعل له ما به يتأتى كماله ويتسنى معاشه

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani reads the verse as God forming the body to receive the perfect spirit, which is ready for every perfection.
rows.anchor: وقال القاشاني : انشأ ظاهرك فعدل بنيتك على وجه قبلت بمزاجه اخاص الروح الأتم

rows.speaker: النجمي
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading says each thing is proportioned to receive its prepared share of divine effusion according to its innate capacity.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية خلق كل شي بحسب الوجود فسوى تسوية بها يصل الفيض الإلهي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reading says creatures share an equal basic creation but differ because some are specially granted guidance.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : خلق الخلق فسوى بينهم في الخلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God measured the kinds, individuals, qualities, acts, lifespans, forms, fortune, guidance, food, and every other feature of creation.
rows.anchor: قدر أجناس الأشياء وأنواعها وأفرادها ومقاديرها وصفاتها وأفعالها وآجالها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says God measured creation fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه اسلام ، إن الله قدر مقادير الخلق قبل أن يخلق السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides each creature toward its natural or chosen function by creating inclinations, inspiration, signs, and revealed verses.
rows.anchor: فوجه كل واحد منها إلى ما يصدر عنه وينبغي له طبعا أو اختيارا ويسره لما خلق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation's guidance appears in instinctive animal behavior, including a weasel catching a mouse and elaborate nest-building by spiders and bees.
rows.anchor: والعنكبوت تبنى بيتها على وجه عجيب غير مقدور والبشر لا يقدر على بناء البيت المسدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ants store food and split damp seeds so they will not sprout, then bring them into the sun to dry.
rows.anchor: والنمل تسعى لأعداد الذخيرة لنفسها فإذا أحست بنداوة المكان تشق الحبة نصفين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An observer recounts a diving bird repeatedly losing its fish to a crow, then dragging the crow underwater and escaping.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم رأيت غواصا وهو طائر غاص وطلع بسمكة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report warns against watering down milk for sale: a monkey exposed a dishonest seller by throwing the water's price into the sea.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث لا تشوبوا اللبن بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says a victim's dog repeatedly uncovered the well where its murdered owner lay, leading to the killer's confession and execution.
rows.anchor: وفي عجائب المخلقوت إن شخصا قتل شخصا بأصفهان وألقاه في بئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Palm trees can become enamored of another tree, weakening and bearing less; binding a branch from the beloved tree to it cures the condition.
rows.anchor: ومن عجيب شجرة النخل أن يعرض لها العشق وهي أن تميل إلى نخلة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pasture is the tender growth God brings forth for grazing animals, in varied colors; Ibn Abbas calls it green herbage.
rows.anchor: أي أنبت بكمال قدرته ما ترعاه الدواب غضا طريقا من بين أخضر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains al-mar'a as green fodder.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه ، المرعى الكلأ الأخضر

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari defines ghutha as flood-borne scraps and rubbish, and qumash as things collected from here and there.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري الغثاء بالضم والمد ما يحمله السيل من القماش والقمش جمع الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When pasture dries, it turns black whether heat or cold caused the withering; the quick sequence hints at the world's short life and fading pleasure.
rows.anchor: أسود من الحوة بمعنى السواد وذلك أن الكلأ إذا جف ويبس أسود سواء كان جفافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet received knowledge without learning to write and became a source of knowledge about writing, its rules, and crafts; God knows what is manifest and hidden.
rows.anchor: من غير تعلم الخط وكان منبع الكمالات كلها حتى إنه علم الكتاب الخط وقوانينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lets the Prophet forget what should be forgotten and preserves what should remain, according to the interests of religion.
rows.anchor: فينسى ما يشاء إنساءه ويبثقى محفوظا ما يشاء إبقاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the Prophet's path easy in every religious matter, enabling reception of revelation, knowledge and teaching of the law, and guidance of others.
rows.anchor: {ونيسرك لليسرى} عطف على نقرئك واليسرى فعلى من اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording makes the Prophet himself easy for the path, signaling such strong mastery and ability that ease becomes a settled trait.
rows.anchor: للإيذان بقوة تمكينه عليه السلام من اليسرى والتصرف فيها بحيث صار ذلك ملكة رسخة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to remind concerns people who may benefit; the Prophet should not exhaust himself on those whose hearts are sealed and who only grow more hostile.
rows.anchor: بأن يخص التذكير بمدار النفع في الجملة بأن يكون من يذكره كلا أو بعضا ممن يرجى منه التذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kashf al-Asrar commentary reads the Arabic particle as an affirmative emphasis, effectively meaning that remembrance does benefit believers when they are prepared to receive it.
rows.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" أن تجيء في العربية مثبتة لا لشرط

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani says the statement if the reminder benefits is a concise transition, expanded by the next verse's account of who will remember.
rows.anchor: قال القاشاني : أجمل في قوله إن نفعت الذي تم فصل بقوله {سيذكر من يخشى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear God, even if only somewhat, will soon remember, reflect, recognize the truth of the reminder, and believe.
rows.anchor: من شأنه أن يخشى الله حق خشيته أو من يشخى الله في الجملة فيزداد ذلك بالتذكير

rows.speaker: صاحب التفسير الكبير
rows.claim: The Great Commentary divides people on resurrection into certain believers, uncertain people open to persuasion, and determined deniers; the first two benefit from reminder.
rows.anchor: وفي التفسير الكبير الناس في أمر المعاد على ثلاثة أقسام منهم من قطع بصحته ومنهم من جوز وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched turns away from the reminder and refuses to listen receptively; this may denote especially hostile leaders or all unbelievers as worse than sinners.
rows.anchor: {ويتجنبها} أي يتبعد من الذكرى ولا يسمعها سماع القبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a hypocrite refused to trade a date palm for one in Paradise, so Uthman gave the petitioner his own orchard and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وروى أن من يخشى هو عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه وإلا شقى رجل من المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two related stories contrast a man who chose eighty sheep over Paradise with an old woman who preferred Paradise to a hundred sheep for revealing Joseph's bones to Moses.
rows.anchor: ونظيره إن رجلا قضى النبي عليه السلام حاجة فقال ائتني بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greater fire can mean the lowest, hottest layer of Hell, where Pharaoh's people, hypocrites, and those who rejected Jesus' table are placed.
rows.anchor: أي يدخل الطبقة السفلى من طبقات النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation compares the great fire of the afterlife with the lesser fire of this world, which is only one seventieth of Hell's fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل الكبرى نار جهنم والصغرى نار الدنيا يعني إن المفضل نار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the greater punishment of the Hereafter, with worldly and barzakh punishment as the lesser punishment.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : الظهر إن المراد بالنار الكبرى هو العذاب الأكبر

rows.speaker: بعض الحكماء
rows.claim: A sage lists gluttony, excessive sleep, persistent sin, hardness of heart, forgetting God, and facing the Almighty as signs of wretchedness.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الحكماء علامة الشقاوة أشياء كثيرة الأكل والشرب والنوم والإصرار على الذنب

rows.speaker: النجمي
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading calls worldly attachment to desires the lesser fire and describes the afterlife's greater fire as abandonment, loss, expulsion, and estrangement.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : النار ناران نار حجاب الدنيا بالاشتغال بالشهوات والذات وهي الصغرى

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani describes greater fire as veiling from God through association and attachment, divine coercion in attributes, wrath in acts, and enduring punishments across four spiritual realms.
rows.anchor: وقال القاشاني : النار الكبرى هي نار الحجاب عن الرب بالشرك والوقوف مع الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned neither die to rest nor live a life that benefits them; then marks a further stage of severity, with existing between life and death worse than burning alone.
rows.anchor: حتى يستريح {ولا يحيى} حياة تنفعه كما يقال

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says they do not die and escape the pain of separation, nor live and attain the relief of union.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء لا يموت فيستريح من غم القطعية ولا يحيي فيصل إلى روح الوصلة

rows.speaker: النجمي
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading says the self is not annihilated to end the veil's punishment and the heart cannot live by faith in the abode of recompense.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : لا يموت نفسه بالكلية ليستريح من عقوبات الحجاب

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani says the spirit cannot cease to exist, yet spiritual ruin deprives it of true life, so it is repeatedly revived for endless punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال القاشاني : لا يموت لامتناع انعدامه ولا يحيي بالحقيقة لهلاكه الروحاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that the damned remain in bodily and spiritual torment; true human life follows death to the self, unlike merely animal life.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير لا يموت لأن الموت يذبح فلا موت ولا يحيى لأن المموم كالميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful escapes harm and gains what is hoped for by purifying from unbelief and sin through the reminder, or by growing in piety and fear.
rows.anchor: أي نجا من المكروه وظفر بما يرجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word qad prepares listeners, after hearing about the fate of those who turn away, to hear the good outcome of those who remember.
rows.anchor: وكلمة قد لما أن عند ابار بسوء حال المتجنب عن الذكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God's name means inwardly and outwardly; prayer means the five prescribed prayers, beginning with the opening takbir, while Hanafi usage includes all forms of remembrance.
rows.anchor: {وذكر اسم ربه} بقلبه ولسانه {فصلى} أقام الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam orders the deeds as purifying false beliefs, recalling knowledge of God through His names and attributes, and serving through prayer and bodily obedience.
rows.anchor: قال الامام مراتب أعمال المكلف ثلاث فأولاها إزالة العقائد الفاسدة عن القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better in its pure, lasting pleasure; worldly pleasure is temporary and mixed with harm, so preferring it merits rebuke.
rows.anchor: حال من فاعل تؤثرون مؤكدة للتوبيخ والعتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outer appearance of things is like a shell and inner realities like a kernel: the kernel lasts, while the discarded shell quickly perishes.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن ظواهر الأشياء بالنسبة إلى حقائقها كالقشر بالنسبة إلى اللب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People devoted to outward appearances prefer fleeting, inferior things because they are veiled from the Hereafter; people of inner truth choose the lasting life with God.
rows.anchor: القشر يؤثرون الأمور الظاهر الخسيسة الدنية الفنية على الأمور الباطنة المعنوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss says the purified person repents, hears the call to prayer, and goes out to pray; the next verse rebukes those who choose worldly work instead.
rows.anchor: ويقال قد أفلح من تزكى أي من تاب من الذنوب وذكر اسم ربه يعني إذا سمع الأذان خرج إلى الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife's reward and purification of the soul, completion of knowledge and obedience, and warning against worldly distraction are truths shared by earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما ذكر من قوله تعالى : {قد أفلح من تزكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier scrolls include those of Abraham and Moses; sahifa means a sheet or written page, while mushaf is a collection of written sheets.
rows.anchor: {صحف} جدك {إبراهيم} الخليل عليه السلام صحف أخيك {موسى} الكليم عليه السلام بدل من الصحف الأولى

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub takes the question as a statement: the account of the Overwhelming Event has already come to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال قطرب من أئمة النحو أي قد جاءك يا محمد حديث الغاشية

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abu al-Su'ud rejects that reading: the question expresses wonder and eagerness to hear an extraordinary account worth transmitting and receiving.
rows.anchor: قال المولى أبو السعود رحمه الله في "الإرشاد" وليس بذاك بل هو استفهام أريد به التعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghashiya is a tremendous calamity that envelops people in hardship from every side, namely the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: والغاشية الداهية الشديدة التي تغشى الناس بشدائدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following description of humbled faces answers the question, with the Day of the Event governing three descriptions; humility and abasement appear on the face.
rows.anchor: وجوه يومئذ خاشعة} استئناف وقع جوابا عن سؤال نشأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces belong to unbelievers, as the traits that follow show; the wording treats faces as their owners because humiliation appears visibly in the face.
rows.anchor: والمراد بأصحابا لوجوه هم الكفار بدلالة ماب عده من الأوصاف
